newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks roar back to end higher.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks roar back to end higher.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks roared back from big early losses to end higher Monday but investors remained worried that the Federal Reserve would boost interest rates next week.
The revamped Dow Jones industrial average rose 20.02 points to 6,955.48 after recovering from a loss of more than 80 points.
But the broader market was mostly lower. Declining issues beat advances by 1,626 to 843 on active volume of 494 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Monday's trading marked the debut of four new components in the 30-stock Dow, as the world's most closely watched stock index became less smokestack- and more technology-oriented.

Added to the list were computer maker Hewlett-Packard, drug maker Johnson & Johnson, Wal-Mart Stores Inc. and insurance company Travelers Group Inc. Dropped were Bethlehem Steel, Westinghouse Electric, Texaco and Woolworth Corp.

The Nasdaq composite index, laced with technology stocks, fell 13.54 points, or 1.05 percent, to 1,279.43. Among leading high-tech names, Intel Corp. shed 1-1/2 to 136-3/8 and International Business Machines fell 4-1/8 to 139-1/2.
The weakness in the broader market underscored how eager investors were to take profits before the March 25 meeting of Fed policy-makers, analysts said.
High tech stocks "have lost momentum and nobody's willing to step up here," said Guy Truicko, equity portfolio manager at Unity Management. "All eyes are on next week's Fed meeting."
Indeed, investors were gripped by nervousness about interest rates, as Wall Street sensed that the odds favoured a rise in short-term rates by the central bank to ward off inflation.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury fell 6/32, raising its yield to 6.96 percent from 6.94 percent at Friday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

In a sign of stocks' sensitivity to interest rates, the Dow index rebounded sharply in late trading when the 30-year Treasury bond rebounded after briefly hitting the psychologically important 7 percent level. Long-term bond yields of 7 percent tend to draw funds from stocks to bonds.
Wall Street was rattled from the opening by billionaire financier Warren Buffett's comment in an annual letter to stockholders that most stocks are over-valued.
"Buffett is a sage a lot of people take to heart," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co.
Harry Laubscher, an analyst at Tucker Anthony said that stocks tend to rise heading into a triple expiration of equity and index options and index futures, which is due on Friday.
"I would anticipate some firmness but nothing getting out of hand because people are still concerned about what happens next week," he said.
Among the new stocks in the Dow index, Hewlett-Packard rose 1/4 to 55-5/8, Travelers lost 1-3/8 to 51-7/8, Johnson & Johnson ended unchanged at 57-7/8 and Wal-Mart rose 1/4 to 28-7/8.
Wall Street was hit by a wave of merger-related news.

Tyco International Ltd. said it was acquiring ADT Ltd. in a stock deal valued at $5.4 billion. Tyco, a maker of fire and safety systems, fell two to 58-1/4. ADT, a maker of electronic security services, gained 3-7/8 to 25-5/8.

H.F. Ahmanson & Co. raised its bid for Great Western Financial in an offer that it said topped a rival "white knight" bid by Washington Mutual Savings Bank. Washington Mutual said it was not planning to raise its offer, adding it was confident its deal would prevail.
Ahmanson fell 1/2 to 39-3/4. Great Western slipped 1/4 to 45-1/4, while Washington Mutual ended up 3/4 to 51-1/8.
Credit card company Advanta Corp. sank 8-1/2 to 31-7/8 after it surprised Wall Street with news that it expects to post a first-quarter loss.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 2.54 points to 795.71. The American Stock Exchange index was off 4.23 at 596.24.
The NYSE composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.67 to 418.37. The average share was down 7 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,576.673 down 4.257 or 0.06 percent.
